gaps.sentence: The storm did considerable ___ to the harbour wall.
gaps.explanation: 'Do damage' — uncountable; 'damages' means money awarded in court.

gaps.sentence: The new regulations came into ___ last month.
gaps.explanation: 'Come into effect' means to start being used; 'affect' is a verb and cannot follow 'into'.

gaps.hint: past participle after 'have'; the verb takes no object
gaps.explanation: 'Rise' (rise, rose, risen) takes no object: sales have risen. 'Raise' takes an object: they raised prices.

gaps.sentence: One of the bolts had worked ___ in the vibration.
gaps.explanation: 'Work loose' = become untightened; 'lose' is the verb for misplacing.

gaps.sentence: The company has changed ___ logo twice.
gaps.explanation: 'Its' is the possessive form of 'it'; 'it's' means 'it is' or 'it has'. 'Its'' does not exist.

gaps.sentence: The committee will ___ your application at its May meeting.
gaps.explanation: The finite verb slot needs 'consider'; 'considerable' means large.

gaps.sentence: Teenagers ___ hours every day on social media.
gaps.hint: to use time or money on something (neutral)
gaps.explanation: 'Spend time/money on something' is the neutral verb for using time or money; 'waste' implies useless use.

gaps.sentence: We had great ___ at the beach party.
gaps.explanation: 'Fun' is an uncountable noun meaning enjoyment; 'funny' is an adjective meaning causing laughter.
